items.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998
items.q: But it was all top notch musicians, and Georgie Auld on tenor and clarinet was —

ctx.x: Now when your first opportunity to record came up, you had kind of an interesting, if my facts are correct, it was kind of an interesting combination of people. Was it Leonard Feather?

Yeah, the pianist didn’t show up so Leonard Feather had to play piano. And it was Georgie Auld on tenor, and it was, the bassist was, his son is named Pickles, I can’t think of his name right now. But it was all top notch musicians, and Georgie Auld on tenor and clarinet was —
